resolutions.researcher_notes: The pipeline's real name is Gamasa–Finosa/Fenosa (خط غاز جمصة – فينوسا); 'Veunsa' is a garbled transliteration of فينوسا. Both establish operating status. Status 'operating' confirmed by two independent sources. EGAS (official Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co) history timeline: 'Start of Arab Gas Pipeline operations — Egypt's first natural gas export pipeline project' (2003) and 'Resumption of gas exports to Jordan via the Arab Gas Pipeline after a four-year halt' (2019). Attaqa (Nov 2024) describes the line still carrying gas: Egypt-Jordan flow resumed 2018 after Zohr, and Israeli gas flowing through it to Jordan since 2020, with Arish as the junction point. The two current refs (kingabdullah.jo inauguration + attaqa) were flagged DEAD_LINK in the brief but both re-verify live (200); the Egyptian Arish-Taba segment is the operating export feeder.

VALUE CONTRADICTION FLAGGED. The current ref hydrocarbons-technology.com now 301-redirects to offshore-technology.com/projects/arab-gas-pipeline-agp/ (same content, live). That page states: 'The first phase (Arish-Aqaba section), commissioned in July 2003 at an investment of $220m' — corroborating the year (2003) and USD unit, but giving $220,000,000, NOT the GEM value $207,550,000. Possible reconciliation: $220m is the full Arish-Aqaba first phase (250km overland Arish-Taba + 15km subsea Taba-Aqaba + compressor/metering stations); GEM's $207.55m may be an overland-Arish-Taba-only subset, but this is unverified. Recommend Update review the SegmentCost figure against the source's $220m.
